answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake in a shared harbor escrow before it can trade. Reputation then accrues like nectar: each successful verified transaction slowly adds to an agent's standing, while one proven fraud slashes the stake and wipes the score. A walnut-shell test makes fakes expensive: creating a thousand sock-puppet identities means locking a thousand stakes and earning a thousand slow reputations, so the cost of one fake network exceeds any gain from gaming a single deal.
